item.title: What it means to be a Greek-Cypriot?
item.description: Published in the Cyprus-Mail, May 17th 2015. In the case of Cyprus one must distinguish between the dual-meaning and usage of the dominant cultural identity. The identity and label of the Greek Cypriot (GC) can have two completely different meanings: there is a constitutional (civic) definition and a cultural definition. The civic definition is that which is found in the 1960 constitution of the Republic of Cyprus, where a GC is a member of the Greek national group.

item.title: Multiculturalism contra Ethnicity: the case of Cyprus
item.description: In late June, I will be presenting a paper titled ‘Multiculturalism contra Ethnicity: the case of Cyprus’ at a conference organised by Surrey’s Center of Research on Nationalism, Ethnicity and Multiculturalism and UCL’s Migration Research Unit, called The Future of Multiculturalism: Structures, Integration Policies and Practices. This is the abstract of my paper: This paper will use the post-conflict and post-colonial multicultural challenges that exist in Cyprus to assess the use of ethnicity as a marker for cultural identification.

item.title: The Borken Olive Branch
item.description: I have almost finished reading the two volume work of Harry Anastasiou The Broken Olive Branch. I will provide a summary in a few posts time (the next one to follow will be Tariq Modood’s Multiculturalism: a Civic Idea)
